key_insight: PlayGround makes graphic layout generation more adaptive by planning progressively while looking at the rendered design, instead of locking in a fixed plan upfront. This helps layouts evolve in response to what the model has already created.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of generating editable graphic designs that stay coherent as visual and text elements are arranged, while avoiding rigid pre-planned workflows that cannot adapt during refinement.
method: Uses a progressive layout generation framework that builds designs step by step rather than all at once.
Grounds planning in rendered visual feedback, so later layout decisions can respond to the current state of the design.
Supports iterative generation and refinement to better match real design workflows while preserving editability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the practicality of design-generation systems by making them more flexible, interactive, and robust to changes during creation. It is especially useful for tools that need editable outputs and human-in-the-loop refinement.
visual_elements: A before-vs-after diagram comparing fixed planning vs progressive planning
A pipeline flowchart showing generate → render → inspect → re-plan → refine
An icon-based illustration of text boxes, images, and editable layout components
A feedback loop graphic highlighting render-grounded planning
paper_title: PLAYGROUND: Progressive Layout Generation with Render-Grounded Planning
paper_authors: Jaeho Lee, Junhwan Heo, Junghyun Park, WonJun Moon, Eunju Yang
